data.long_meaning: Osvaldo is derived from the Latin name Oswald, meaning 'wealth-ruler'. In the Anglo-Saxon language, it is derived from Oswald, meaning 'divine power' or 'God power'. Oswald is a powerful name, symbolizing both wealth and divine power. It is a name that inspires courage, strength, and faith. The name Osvaldo carries the meaning “Wealth-Ruler” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Latin. Parents who choose Osvaldo usually hope their child will grow to embody wealth-ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Osvaldo I of Asturias, also known as Osvaldo the Great, was a son of Alfonso II of Asturias and Ermesinda of Carrión. He was born around 817 and became king of Asturias in 824, during the Muslim occupation of the Iberian Peninsula. During his reign, he successfully defended against several Muslim raids and expanded his kingdom, reaching the area of modern-day León. He died in 850.

historical_references.reference: Osvaldo of Canosa, also known as Osvaldo the Good, was a Norman nobleman who lived in southern Italy in the late 11th century. He was the count of Canosa and a vassal of the Norman prince Robert Guiscard. Osvaldo led the Norman army in the conquest of Apulia and Calabria, and later became the Duke of Apulia in 1057. He was a just ruler and is remembered for his good governance and generosity.
